text:
anna: thinking about a lighter-weight handback for canaries where latency is the main signal. idea: prioritize quick degradation paths that avoid full rollback when p95 spikes but error-rate is low.

sam: +1. are you imagining traffic split change or routing to a degraded model?

anna: routing to degraded model by default — cheaper model or quantized variant — but keep a tiny mirror to the canary for quality sampling. less blast radius.

lee: ops concern: sticky sessions. if we move half of traffic to degraded model, sessions might break. we need session-affinity aware handback.

jordan: we can do per-request routing by header or cookie. runtime has affinity-key support already. just need to expose a handback policy in rollout config.

anna: proposal sketch (pseudo-yaml):
```yaml
canary_policy:
  metrics:
    latency_p95_threshold_ms: 350
    errors_ratio_threshold: 0.02
  actions:
    - type: graceful_reroute
      target: degraded_variant
      preserve_affinity: true
      mirror_sampling: 0.02
    - type: full_rollout_pause
      notify: oncall
```

sam: love the mirror_sampling. keeps evals honest. also: add a cooldown window so we don't oscillate.

lee: add circuit-breaker semantics too. if degraded_variant also fails, escalate. we should failover to last-known-good region or denylist specific model.

nina: product question: how do we ensure graceful_reroute preserves user-visible quality? sampling alone might miss rare regressions.

anna: good point — tie sampling to user cohorts and prompt buckets. keep a small set of critical prompts that are always mirrored.

jordan: implementation notes: rollout-controller should expose a simple DSL for these policies. controller evaluates telemetry stream and emits route-deltas to the router service. router implements quick-path reroute with <1s convergence.

ci-bot: deploy pipeline report: rollout-controller v0.9 passed canary tests in staging. tests: latency-injection, partial-degradation.

sam: ops checklist for handback: add runbook step to confirm mirror logs, run automated eval against critical prompts, verify affinity headers preserved.

lee: alerting: create a composite alert: (p95 > threshold AND error_rate > small_threshold) OR repeated reroute_count > 3 in 10m. that reduces noise.

anna: tradeoffs: - quicker user impact mitigation vs potential silent quality regressions. need strong observability.

jordan: telemetry needs: per-variant token-cost, tail latency histogram, sample-based quality delta (BLEU/embedding-sim). we'll wire to console dashboards.

nina: agree to own a small evaluation harness that runs 200 critical prompts against both variants every 2m. will publish pass/fail metric.

sam: timeline? can we ship controller + router hook in 3 sprints if we scope minimal: policy DSL, reroute op, mirror sampling?

anna: 3 sprints seems reasonable. i'll draft an RFC with config examples, runbook snippet, and safety knobs. will @sam and @lee for review.

lee: ping me once RFC lands. I'll add oncall playbook and the alert definitions.

jordan: i'll stub the dashboard and expose the agent metrics.

ci-bot: note: please add integration test that asserts affinity header survives reroute.

anna: thanks all — RFC in #docs/rfcs tomorrow. tagging follow-ups: ownership, test matrix, rollout simulation harness. :thumbsup:
